title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We quantify the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier plus a single automated repair iteration into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Following a preregistered paired design (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026), we generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters and used shared_initial_candidate semantics so that each task produced one LLM proposal that both conditions evaluated. Requested model: gpt-5-mini; validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000; seed = 1729). The archived exact McNemar two-sided implementation treats the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 and computes a two-sided p-value via the Binomial(n, 0.5) distribution; for the observed n = 1 we report p = 1.00. Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the marginal numeric verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, although the guarded loop corrected at least one concrete baseline failure (the single discordant episode is archived and locatable deterministically in execution/raw_results.jsonl). All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being investigated for operational NetOps tasks: intent-to-configuration translation, change planning, and automated repair. System reports and surveys emphasise that operational safety is shaped heavily by engineering safeguards—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than by the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A widely proposed mitigation is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the model generates a configuration candidate, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and repairs are applied when violations appear. Despite conceptual consensus, controlled, artifact-backed measurements isolating a verifier’s marginal contribution while holding the model’s initial proposal fixed remain limited in the public literature. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired experiment that answers a narrowly scoped operational question: given identical initial proposals, how much does integrating a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback?
sections.related_work: Network-configuration verification methods (header-space analysis and route-model verifiers) provide deterministic checks for reachability, isolation, and update-safety and underpin many NetOps verification tools [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems instantiate LLM-based intent translators and emphasize validators and guardrails to reach operational reliability (e.g., INTA and Confucius system reports) [Wei et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair and critic-in-the-loop patterns are advocated across structured-generation domains to reduce incorrect outputs and produce machine-checkable artifacts [PoeTone; INTA]. Studies of LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) motivate verifier-in-the-loop pipelines and guardrails [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. However, the supplied literature seldom reports controlled ablations that quantify the verifier’s effect size under reproducible, preregistered conditions; this work contributes one such artifact-backed measurement and situates its conditional scope relative to those prior systems.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design: The study preregistration (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026; archived SHA-256 = 405a9f882cbf...334d) froze the confirmatory hypothesis, inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generation seeds, estimands, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to execution. Confirmatory hypothesis H1: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will yield a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired per task). The preregistered primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations.

Task generation and strata: We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds to produce 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified into VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166) clusters. Each task payload constrained allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan} to align construct validity with the deterministic validator’s modeled features; tasks referencing unmodeled features would be routed to an 'unmodeled-feature' cohort and excluded from the primary analysis (no such exclusions occurred).

Generation semantics and controlled contrast: To isolate the verifier+repair marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false: for each task a single shared LLM proposal (the shared candidate) was produced and served as the baseline output; the guarded condition evaluated that identical shared candidate with the deterministic validator and invoked a repair-stage call only if the validator reported preregistered high/medium-severity violations. This semantic prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration strategies and isolates the marginal corrective effect of verification plus one repair iteration conditional on an identical model proposal.

Models, adapter, and validator: The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider: openai_responses). The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator specification and violation-code→severity mapping are archived in the execution artifacts. The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Primary statistical test and exact implementation: The preregistered confirmatory test was McNemar’s paired test on binary outcomes. The archived executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar test by reducing to an exact Binomial(n, 0.5) on the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 and computing the two-sided p-value as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0. With the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n = 1) both one-sided tail probabilities equal 0.5, so the two-sided p = 1.00. This computational rule and rationale are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We also computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the absolute difference using B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) where each resample draws 500 paired tasks with replacement, preserving pairing.

Missingness, retries and stopping: Preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automated retries for transient provider errors; stopping rule ended the run when the preregistered confirmatory pairs (N = 500) completed or when the adapter’s model-call budget was reached. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501 and completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 pairs × 2 condition evaluations under shared-initial semantics with one repair call). All provider-call traces, prompts, responses, and retry metadata are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes: The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500, model_calls_used = 501, and observed repair-stage provider calls = 1. Per-condition aggregated counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar two-sided p and bootstrap CI: Applying the archived exact binomial rule on discordant pairs (n = 1) yields two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000; seed = 1729). These artifacts appear in analysis/results.json and associated CSVs.

Repair activity and discordant-pair provenance: Exactly one repair-stage call occurred and that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1)—i.e., the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The discordant episode and its validator diagnostics, repair prompt/response, and provider-call trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl; the episode is deterministically locatable by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. Because exactly one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this filter returns the single episode and its repair-stage provider-call trace for qualitative inspection. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is provided in the validator-spec artifacts in the evidence bundle.

Secondary and subgroup analyses: The preregistered per-violation-class secondary analyses were not informative because observed violation counts were nearly zero; there were no substantive counts to support class-level inference. The preregistration anticipated an approximate baseline prevalence p_b ≈ 0.30 for power planning; the observed prevalence (1/500 failures) was far lower. This ceiling effect invalidates the power assumption and explains the small observed absolute effect and lack of statistical significance under the two-sided exact-binomial convention used.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the constrained, verifier-scoped regime tested—one requested model (gpt-5-mini), deterministic shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic validator modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and a single automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measurable benefit of verifier+single-repair on the pass-rate metric was small (0.002). Nevertheless, the guarded loop corrected at least one concrete baseline failure (the archived discordant episode), demonstrating corrective potential even in a ceiling regime.

Design-choice implications: The shared_initial_candidate semantics were a deliberate preregistered choice to isolate verifier+repair conditional on identical proposals; this answers an operational question different from those addressed by verifier-guided regeneration or iterative repair strategies. If an operator’s deployment semantics prefer minimizing total model calls or preserving the model's original proposal, the G→V→R shared-initial design is the appropriate measurement. If the deployment goal is strictly maximal final-pass probability regardless of call budget, verifier-guided regeneration with higher repair budgets may yield larger absolute gains.

Threats to validity: Internal validity benefits from the preregistered paired design, deterministic seeds, automatic exclusion rules, and zero manual adjudication. Construct validity depends on whether the verifier’s modeled property set aligns with operational safety concerns; our pass/fail outcome is relative to the verifier’s property and severity mapping. External validity is limited: a single model family and a single validator were tested on a synthetic corpus constrained to three fields; results do not show cross-vendor or multi-model generality. Conclusion validity: the extremely low baseline failure rate produced a ceiling effect that substantially reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements; the preregistered power calculation assumed a far higher baseline error prevalence, so the run is underpowered for the observed base rate.

Operational recommendations grounded in the archive: (1) Measure baseline proposal-error prevalence on representative operational data before committing to expensive repair budgets—if baseline error is near-zero, marginal pass-rate gains from costly verifier+repair pipelines may be small for the pass-rate metric. (2) Ensure verifier coverage aligns with operator-critical properties: inspect the archived validator-spec and violation-code mapping. (3) Select generation semantics (shared-initial vs verifier-guided regeneration) to match operational priorities; the evidence bundle contains exemplar repair traces and provider-call accounting to estimate cost–benefit tradeoffs.

Reproducibility notes (artifact-grounded): All preregistration, the task-generator code and seeds, model-configuration, provider-call traces, raw LLM responses, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, execution logs, and analysis CSVs are archived in the evidence bundle under execution/* and analysis/*. Key artifact summaries: execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; max_output_tokens = 2000), execution/raw_results.jsonl (input_results_sha256 = e7c1fc4d...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 = 5908...), and analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 = 81f1...). The precise initial master prompt for this autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM proposals were nearly perfect for the verifier-scoped task set (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]) and an archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 using the executor’s Binomial(n, 0.5) convention on discordant pairs. This measurement documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal error prevalence is extremely low and verifier coverage is constrained, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a verifier on this metric may be negligible—yet the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures (one archived correction in this run). Operators should measure baseline proposal error and align verifier coverage and generation semantics with operational priorities; the evidence bundle supports deterministic re-inspection of every claim and exemplar in this paper.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}, so results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents or vendor-specific CLI heterogeneity.
Single model family requested (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or verifier-guided regeneration strategies could materially change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) produced a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s Binomial(n, 0.5) two-sided convention for n = 1 discordant pair.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl; it is deterministically locatable by filtering that file for the unique pair where baseline pass == 0 and guarded pass == 1.
